componentPlan.focusQuote: At its core, the water cycle is the motion of the water from the ground to the atmosphere and back again.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Labels ground, atmosphere and water stores to orient students before sequencing processes.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Evaporation of this runoff into the atmosphere begins the hydrologic cycle over again.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Orders evaporation through runoff in cycle order to show continuous circulation.

overview.headline: Water moves continuously between Earth and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the hydrologic cycle involves continuous circulation of water between Earth and atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that evaporation is a change of state from liquid substance to gas.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration is evaporation of water from plants through stomata.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation changes water vapor into liquid and releases heat energy.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation includes rain, hail, snow and sleet falling to Earth.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that runoff occurs when saturated ground cannot absorb more water.
keyPoints.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: Change of liquid substance into gas that needs energy
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: Evaporation of water from plants through leaf stomata
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: Small openings on leaves connected to plant tissues
keyTerms.quote: Stomata are small openings found on the underside of leaves that are connected to vascular plant tissues.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where water vapor changes into liquid clouds or dew
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: Water falling as rain, hail, snow or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Excess water that saturated ground cannot absorb
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains the hydrologic cycle and its main processes of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation and runoff with everyday examples.
analysis.subject: earth-science
